response.content:
## Nordic Forestry Automation (NFA)

### What the company does
Nordic Forestry Automation (NFA) is a physical-AI company that develops software and sensor-based operator-support systems for forestry harvesting machines. Its technology uses a sensor stack (LiDAR, GNSS, cameras, IMU) combined with onboard Nvidia compute and AI algorithms to create a real-time digital map of trees and their surroundings. This helps machine operators thin and harvest forests more precisely while reducing cognitive load. The system can be retrofitted to any type of forest harvester. NFA's first product — an operator support system for thinning — is deployed commercially across seven markets on three continents. The company is also developing next-generation features including tree species identification, stem shape measurement, and semi-automation capabilities.

### Headquarters
**Lund, Sweden** (Scheelevägen 15, 223 70 Lund)

### Employees
Specific employee headcount data is not publicly available.

### Funding

| Round | Date | Amount | Lead Investors |
|---|---|---|---|
| Seed | Jul 2023 | ~SEK 10M (~$980K) | Södra Ädla, Sveaskog, Almi Invest Syd |
| Early-stage VC | Jun 2026 | SEK 48M (~€4.3M / ~$4.9M) | Navigare Ventures, Almi Invest GreenTech |

- **Total funding raised:** approximately **$5M** (disclosed) across two rounds.
- **Latest round (Jun 2026):** SEK 48 million (~$4.9M), led by Navigare Ventures and Almi Invest GreenTech, with LRF Ventures joining as a new minority owner and follow-on participation from Sveaskog, Södra Skogsägarna, and Almi Invest Syd. This was described as one of Sweden's largest forestry-tech rounds.

### Additional context
- **Founded:** 2021, as a spinout from KTH Royal Institute of Technology
- **Founders:** Lars Svensson (CEO) and David Gillsjö (from the WASP programme)
- **Industries:** Software & Services, Machinery, AI, Robotics, Forestry

context.content: “Forest thinning is a craft that requires 100-percent focus and takes several years to master. The total cognitive load is comparable to that of a fighter pilot. Sensor-based operator support provides better conditions for operators and forest owners to promote forest values. We are grateful for the opportunity to continue developing this technology together with our new partners,” said Lars Svensson, CEO of NFA. [...] Thinning a forest involves constant decision-making about which, and how many, trees to harvest in order to best promote the various values of the forest. How the thinning operation is carried out is important for the long-term development of the forest, but is usually done manually and based on the experience of each individual operator. To make the thinning task easier, Nordic Forestry Automation (NFA) has developed an AI-based system to continuously support the operator in forest management [...] NFA’s operator support can be retrofitted to any type of forest harvester and supports operators in forest management decisions. The system measures, positions and classifies all trees around the machine automatically and in real time. It also gives the position of the machine and cutting head with centimetre accuracy.
